Unpleasant experience.

frontline_communication.snippet:
Decided to give it a shot on account of the reviews, generally reasonable experiences from people I've met and long lead times for Tesla Service but thus far my personal experience has been quite abject to say the least.

To start, brought a Model Y in for general maintenance on Tuesday morning for rountine maintenance and 4 specfic items listed in the service request submitted the friday prior. During drop off I was informed that a quote would be ready in about 2 hours, but did not hear back until over 6 hours later, 40 min before closing informing me that they were not able to finish a quote that day but next day would be possible. The following day, I was informed around noon that a  quote would not be ready until the day after, and upon requesting an estimate of when the repairs could be completed was not provided a reasonable estimate. This so far is not a great experience but for what occured next.

Upon not reciving a reasonabe estimate as to the timeline of repairs requested or a complete quote, I called in 1.5h ahead and requested my tires be rotated and to make sure there was no miscommunication, submitted the same via text which was confirmed recived when they called back 10 minutes subsequent.

Needless to say, the tires were not rotated.

But wait there's more! My driver's seat also started loudly creaking at the slightest bumps where it had not prior. I suppose, generously, this was because the seat needed to be moved to access the sterring column and the mechanic that did not re-assemble it with due care because they supposed that it would be accessed again before it was picked up but it's  but I'm not sure how much I care.

Overall communcaiton left much to be desired, partial quote provided was >50% over Tesla's and service was neither prompt nor convenient as much as I am sympathetic to staffing gaps the overall value proposition makes no sense as-is even with 1st party wait times. Not being able to provide a tire quote after 2 full days is all pretty crazy for an auto shop.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Repeated delays and conflicting timelines on the quote; poor communication throughout.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
I’ve been going to The Garage for years and generally trusted their work, but my most recent experience left me disappointed.

I brought in my 2019 Acura TLX because two warning lights came on: “Emissions System Problem” and “Electric Parking Brake Problem.” They charged me over $230 for a diagnostic check, and I was surprised to learn that this fee isn’t applied toward the repair if you choose to move forward.

Their recommendation was to replace the part connecting the gas tank to the cap. The quoted price for the part alone was about $450, whereas I found the same part online for around $225 (plus labor). The overall estimate for repair was close to $1,000.

Before agreeing, I got a second opinion from another mechanic, who simply suggested resetting the warning lights first. That’s what I did, and it cost about $225 total. Two weeks later, I’m still driving with no issues and the lights never returned.

When I asked The Garage why both lights would appear at once, they said it’s common for multiple warnings to come on to prevent driving—but several mechanics I spoke with afterward told me they had never heard of that explanation.

It left me feeling like The Garage was recommending a costly repair without fully confirming the root cause. This is disappointing, especially since I’ve trusted them for years. I hope this was just an isolated experience, but it’s worth noting for anyone considering service here.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Diagnostic fee structure was an undisclosed cost the customer found surprising.

I was surprised by how hasty he was so I asked how he knew, and he said that "well I'm a mechanic". Later he gave me an estimate of $1000 to replace the starter. Luckily I decided to take my car to the dealership instead, and turned out the issue was neither the battery nor the starter.

frontline_communication.snippet:
The technicians are good. The older gentleman who worked on my Mercedes really knows his stuff so that's a major benefit . The shop is clean .

The manager Greg is a sometimes nice guy that seems to be moody at times and he can come across almost rude. In fact he's rude so often that I started laughing to myself recently at how tone deaf he seems.  I called him the morning after the evening he sent me notice that my car was done.  He gruffly said that I had had my car there too long. It was less than 12 hours after his evening notice of completion!

I told him I would come in on Monday (the next business day) to pick it up then texted Monday saying I had a medical issue and needed to come in the next day. When I picked up the car as stated, he said gruffly he was going to start charging me storage cost and everything about him seemed annoyed by my presence and that I was his customer. I have been nothing but nice to this guy and spent over 12k on some fairly basic stuff for this classic car.  He said he didn't get my text but that's on him. When I told him that he is sounding rude when I am a paying customer that is spending good money on his services he said we can end our relationship. I didn't know that we had a "relationship"!  Lol!  He softened up after that cuz I think he felt bad but again it's all kind of laughable, his moodiness.

He is personally knowledgeable about these classic cars as he seems to have owned quite a few of them himself. He also seems to rely on AI a lot for his information about cars and it's not always correct so look it up yourself. For example, I wanted to remove the heater covers to get them re-chromed and he said they'll break because they're "pot metal". AI does say that but *not for this car* and if you delve further they are nice forged brass on a 190 SL. They also charged me for removing the chrome parts but they didn't remove the chrome parts entirely that I asked them to despite specific instructions. Also the car was filthy dirty when I came to pick it up, and the rear view mirror was all twisted the wrong Direction and coming out of its seating.  Online it's touted that they wash your vehicle.

Anyway Gregs run a pretty tight ship but I think Greg could learn the old business adage a little better: "the customer is always right."

Especially given the premium prices they charge their customers! (granted they have a premium location in the heart of Russian Hill Polk Street area)

There are alternatives in the City with nicer attitudes and not as expensive.  I may go back to Pete's when needed but I may try some other spots like Sal's in SF.
frontline_communication.reasoning: Manager repeatedly came across as rude and moody to a paying customer.

calls_unanswered.snippet:
I tried calling, leaving voicemails, and texting in order to make an appointment and it took a week for them to get back to me via text. They informed me that they do not work on my particular VW even though the previous owner of the vehicle took it there for years. When I asked what had changed they did not respond (maybe the will get back to me in a week). Maybe they do good work but based on this experience I would take your car and money elsewhere.

Edit: I'm sorry I upset you. I called multiple times for multiple days before texting, that's what I was referring to when I said a week (though it may have been 8 days). Also, you never even asked me what type of work I needed done (you don't do oil changes?) and you never got back to me on what had changed until seeing this review which is a strange way to respond to the question. I'm glad business is going well for you guys and I wish you the best. I found a mechanic closer to me who had no trouble finding the parts and helping me out with general maintenance (and they don't even claim to be European car specialist).
calls_unanswered.reasoning: Repeated calls and voicemails went unanswered for about a week.

billing_or_intake_errors.snippet:
My car got broken into on 8/2. I was out of town so my mom helped to arranged for it to be towed to the shop. She already paid for the towing service which was $217, and Steven claimed $497 and got the check from my insurance.

There was no other damages besides the broken windows. Weeks later, Steven told me that there are some scratches (which were not there when I dropped off the car key). I think these were caused by someone pressing the broken glass to smear them on the car body. He filed for a total $6k+ claim including products and services he quietly added to the estimation for repairing/replacing the body and parts that he vandalized.

I’ve reported this to the national and state bureaus for insurance fraud, and the CA bureau of auto repair along with my insurance’s SIU.

I hope he’s not going to secretly damage my car further because I will have to take legal actions before any bureaus did.
billing_or_intake_errors.reasoning: Charges were quietly added to the estimate without the customer's knowledge.
